needs: Desktop app; a real provider key you can also deliberately break, or included access; a screenshot on the clipboard and a few files to drag.
steps: Hover and tab to the copy control on your own message and on a reply; paste the result somewhere else.
Enter a wrong provider key in Settings and watch the check. Send a message, read the failure, fix the key and choose Try again.
Start a second message while a turn is running and look at whether Try again is offered on an earlier failure.
Paste a screenshot into the composer, then drag two files and a folder onto it. Paste ordinary text and a very long text.
Go offline and send a message; pick a model your key cannot use; read each message and its Details.
Repeat copy and paste in a Task and in the Garden-level console.
proof: Copy puts the full message text on the clipboard and confirms it; it is reachable by keyboard.
A refused key is reported when saved without blocking the save, and a key that cannot be checked is still saved with a clear note.
Try again answers the original request without adding a second copy of my message, and is not offered while something else is running.
A pasted image and dropped files appear in Artifacts with sensible names and are referenced in the message; pasted text stays text; the long-paste behavior is unchanged.
Failures name the next step (fix the key, choose another model, check the connection) with the provider's own wording available under Details.
With AI Tools off none of these controls suggest AI is available.
twist: Paste the same screenshot twice quickly, and drop a file on the composer while the Artifacts panel is also showing a drop target. Nothing should be added twice or lost.

title: Visitors can read the terms and report a creation
goal: As a visitor or customer, I want to know the terms and privacy practices, reach a person, and flag a published creation that should not be there.
needs: The public website (deployed, or the local public candidate with the matching API) and a disposable published creation. A phone-width browser for one pass.
steps: Read Terms, Privacy and Contact in full. Check every statement against what you know the product does, and that no company name, address or email is wrong or invented.
Find the links from the teaser, Explore, a creator page, Plans, the billing return pages, account sign-in in the app, and Settings → Account.
On a published creation, a Tool page and a Mood page, open Report. Submit each reason once, with and without details and email.
Submit reports quickly until you are asked to wait; lose the connection mid-submit.
Try to register the usernames terms, privacy, contact and explore.
Open robots.txt and the sitemap, and share a creation link into a chat app to see its preview.
proof: The legal pages are readable on a phone, dated, and accurate; Contact reaches a real destination.
Terms and Privacy are one click from every place money or an account is involved.
A report is accepted with a clear confirmation; a refusal or failure keeps what I wrote and says what to do.
The operator receives or can list the report with its reason, details and creation.
Reserved names are refused in the app and by the API with a plain reason.
robots.txt and the sitemap resolve and list only listed creations. Record what the chat-app preview shows: a per-creation preview is a known gap.
twist: Report a creation, then have its creator unshare it. The report should still exist for the operator.

title: The operator can remove a creation and sign-in resists abuse
goal: As the operator, I want to act on a report by taking a creation down, keep it down, and know that sign-in codes cannot be spammed.
needs: Full API on a test deployment with an operator account, the reports/takedowns migration applied and TRUST_PROXY set; two test creator accounts; an HTTP client for the admin routes (there is no operator screen yet).
steps: List open reports, then take down a reported creation with a reason. Visit its public address and Explore.
As the creator, try to share the same creation again from the app, and read the message.
Resolve and dismiss reports; lift the takedown and share again.
Request sign-in codes for one email repeatedly, then from two networks; enter wrong codes until refused; request a new code and sign in.
Request a code for an email with no account and compare the answer and timing with a real one.
Confirm two people on different networks are limited independently (this is what TRUST_PROXY provides).
proof: A takedown removes the public creation and its Explore entry, and resolves its open reports.
The creator cannot republish while the takedown is active and is told why in plain words; local work is untouched.
Lifting the takedown allows sharing again.
Code requests and wrong attempts are limited per email and per network with a plain message, and a fresh code recovers.
Answers do not reveal whether an email has an account.
One person's limit never locks out another network.
twist: Take down a creation that has a custom domain and visitor data, then close the creator's account. Note what remains and whether anything is left serving.
